content: “Am I home?” The unfamiliar voice spoke causing Marcus to pause in surprise, that isn’t me is it he wondered, blinking back the painful sunlight, his vision beginning to clear as the green and brown of the cold autumn forest came into focus, looking up he surveyed the surviving leaves playing in the  stiff  breeze as it drifted across the canopy. Earth, he thought as his body began to relax, the deep ache from joints that had not been moved in centuries called to him as he shifted.  Turning ,  he studied the remnants of the silver  teardrop-shaped  craft  half-buried  at the end of a long ravine created when it had hit the ground. How long have I been away? He wondered ,  looking to the surrounding fauna for answers, but none came. Marcus winced as his muscles protested in pain as he moved them, testing his strength. The one-piece  Gortex  outfit he wore stretching with the movements of his body, the restriction of the  gear  causing him to scowl in annoyance.  After such a long period of Cryogenic sleep, your body will require a  period  to adjust . However,  your entire being will be frozen, ensuring you do not age while waiting for your return home we anticipate certain unpleasant side effects that you will have to overcome upon awakening  a familiar voice echoed from his mind, a holdover from his now distant past.  Here I am ,  he thought, a smile replacing the annoyed wince as he studied the lush green landscape before him.  Marcus had spent time in forests, mostly training with the Army, but it had not been a place he had felt at home. In fact, during his time with the Army Corp of Engineers ,  he had spent most of his time in the deserts of Africa, engineering irrigation solutions for small remote areas. The forest ,  though familiar ,  was not the comfort he had hoped it would be.  He continued to sit for a moment, not trusting his muscles to stand, he missed the desert, missed the work, he had been good at it ,  it had been his reputation of solving unsolvable problems that had brought him to the attention of the ARC project. Marcus shook his head as memories flooded his mind, the machine found in the ice, the discovery of its purpose as a weapon and then the  world in  panic, The ARC project had been formed as a  last-ditch  effort ,  desperation a t the thought of the end of  humanity  they had studied the machine, learned from it and then applied some of that technology to allow  humanity  the ability to launch into space and sleep away centuries as it waited for the plant to heal.  “Here I am , ” he said, again the gravelly voice damn near unrecognizable to him. He shook it off as he unsteadily got to his feet. Shuffling over to the ship he leaned down and studied the damage to the hull it isn’t going to fly again he thought walking around the small vessel, the pod that had returned him to the planet . For  a moment he looked up, he imagined he could see the  giant  mothership that hovered in geosynchronous orbit, pods lined up in  their  docks as they waited for the Artificial Intelligence to deem the planet safe and begin launch sequence.  He had spent centuries on board that ship, sleeping, frozen, just waiting for the computer to finally launch him and all his fellow volunteers back to the planet that has birthed humanity. Turning with a start as something large moved through the woods some distance away, he felt fear creep up his back and shambled his way towards the rear of the  teardrop-shaped  ship. He might have been trained as a soldier, but Marcus Gavin had spent his career building and creating, not fighting what few combat skills he had were remnants of the training he had once received in Basic training.  Reaching the back of the small vessel ,  he breathed a sigh relief to see that the rear section had been undamaged. Marcus listened for another tell-tale sign of the  giant  creature in the woods . Still, none  came, Feeling around the surface of the vessel he found the small indent he had been looking for and pushed, a recessed keyboard slid smoothly from the ship ,  and he tapped in a code, waiting patiently as a door slid open, revealing a packed storage compartment. He began pulling out he gear stored there, mostly emergency supplies should he find himself far from civilization, a backpack, a tent, food ,  and stored water ,  all of which he stacked neatly next to the ship.  Reaching into the rear of the compartment ,  Marcus smiled as his hand closed over a large black plastic case. Sliding it out, he opened it to reveal a Military issue carbine and pistol, complete with extra  clips stored nearly in the padded case. Picking up the carbine and a magazine ,  he loaded the weapon, pulling back the charging handle and letting it slam forward, the metal on metal sound of a bullet  chambering  comforting as he moved around the ship and faced the direction of the sound.  After some deliberation, he decided a warning shot would be the most effective and pointed the rifle at a large tree and aimed, squeezing the trigger he was surprised when the only sound was the metallic click. Pulling his cheek off of the stock, he studied the weapon curiously for a moment . He  ejected the round and chambered another, squeezing the trigger, once again ,  was rewarded with a metallic click. “What the hell” he whispered ,  looking at the weapon. His voice sounding at least  semi-normal,  he thought distractedly.  Pulling the magazine, he popped a round out of the magazine and proceeded to rummage around in the overloaded pack until he came out with a small tool case. Carefully he removed the round from the shell and upending the metal casing a small clump of yellowish rock tumbled out of the bullet casing. “Of all the stupid upgrades , ” he chastised no  on , e  in particular, recalling one briefing he remembered the excitement of the engineer when they had revealed that the cordite mixture might not last  century. They  had come up with a solution to that problem.  As Marcus stared at the useless rock in his hand, he simply shook his head ; the  guns were useless he realized and packing it away ,  he began searching the equipment for anything else he could use. Within twenty minutes ,  he had laid out an Ontario K-Bar knife and a survival hatched. Judging by the sound of the thing in the woods, if it  were  hostile ,  this wouldn’t do more than piss it off, he thought ,  but it was better than nothing. He had spent his entire military career being a creator, a problem  solver ,  not a killer, not a destroyer ,  he thought.  Marcus had been the golden boy ; at  the young age of twenty-seven ,  he had a reputation for solving the impossible in the war-torn areas of the globe. If water  needed to flow  in the villages of Africa run by a malevolent warlord,  he would go , before long water would run over crops with the consent of said warlord . Still, private  organizations and even that of his government stood impressed . In  awe of his ability to navigate not only the engineering hardships but the political ones, it was that reputation  that  had earned him a spot on the ARC.   Marcus stripped out of the wet chemical covered  one-piece  outfit and into more traditional army BDU’s doing his best to wipe away the chemicals that covered his body head to do .  He was wet and cold, covered in the gel that had protected his body during the centuries of sleep now a mere annoyance, running a t-shirt over his body Marcus did his best to clean off the solution and restore a feeling of clean.   Standing there clean and dry ,  he took a deep appreciative breath of the  fresh  forest air, he knew the plan, the scenario and was pleased to see the surrounding woods untouched by what they thought would be the end of the planet.  When they had found the machine, the scientists in charge of studying it had not known what it was they had when during an experiment had inadvertently activated the damn thing. It had taken another year to finally figure out what it was that they had turned on and ,  more importantly ,  how to read the countdown that had begun on that fateful day. In their efforts ,  they had lost a year out of six, leaving five years before the machine would destroy  humanity , releasing virulent pathogens and nanite armies to remove humans and their creations.  Shortly  after that ,  the ARC project  began , taking technology learned from the machine, they  started  to build ships, technologies and the process of placing humans in Cryonic sleep, freezing them until such time that they would return. But if Marcus knew that would happen in batches, meaning he wouldn’t be the only one who would have returned ,  he thought, looking around and seeing no sign of another pod or human. He needed information he thought reaching into the pod and from the center of the control system removed a metallic object that looked like a chrome egg, another piece of that altered  technology he thought, placing the small device on the ground as it began to pulse red. Standing and watching it,  Marcus  waited as the red lights turned yellow .  He shivered as the gel chilled in the cold autumn day, Marcus tried to wipe the solution from  h is body, removing as much of it as possible as he pushed the t-shirt over his arms and torso doing his best to feel clean again.  “Sentinel is online Marcus Gavin, by your command , ” the soft female voice stated .  He studied the interface, the body without intelligence of it s own the VI  stood there like a puppet waiting for an operator. It would connect with the ship allowing the Artificial Intelligence a way to communicate with a volunteer personally, giving them the information and guidance needed as they began the journey of rebuilding. It was  a fantastic  piece of technology, this interface ,  and he still had to remember it was  merely  a machine, Marcus could easily associate human feelings and actions to this hologram. But the VI was also his lifeline, his ability to glean information and find others like him ; it  was his lifeline to civilization ,  he thought.  “Sentinel, please review mission and bring me up to speed on the current situation” he stated clearly, as he watched the silhouette froze for a minute, the device communicating and receiving information from the ship, the distance causing a small lag in response he knew. Finally, the VI shook its head “Certainly Marcus , ” it  began,  and the image of the person vanished, forming instead into an image of the planet hanging in front of him. He knew it was from  the ship's archives , the image centuries old, from when the mission began but still seeing Earth and all its lights and people from space caused his breath to pause, it was his home he thought, watching as the planet lazily spun in front of him.  After a moment ,  it began to speed up the AI giving a time-lapsed image . As  Marcus watched, ships launched from the surface . They quickly began  to load into the mothership, that had been the pods, they had loaded everyone into them on earth and then like cargo shipped the frozen volunteers to the mothership, loading them into the berths. The flurry of activity stopped, and the earth continued to spin, the rotation speeding up even more as the AI accelerated the view once again.  Then to Marcus’s horror ,  the lights on the planet began to go out, slow at first and then faster and faster, before long the  earth  was dark, a red mist began to populate the  earth  leaving it in a red haze, he didn’t know what it was . Still, he decided  to wait to ask, instead  of  allowing the visual briefing to continue . Eventually ,  the red  mist  faded as the planet spun, faster and faster. For almost thirty minutes ,  it did it, the  earth  a blur until instantly it slowed ,  and as Marcus watched, pods exploded from the mothership and began to descend to earth, as he watched a second and then a third mothership came into view . Those  two launched its pods, the small metal ships  falling  to earth, then the planet sped up again, slowing once in a while as a random pod launched . It  would speed up again ,  repeating the process a little time later ; this  happened twelve times until a final pod launched, descending to earth ,  and the visual briefing stopped.  Marcus stood there silent as he thought through what he just witnessed, what had he seen, he wondered, playing it back in his head. “Sentinel, what can you tell me about the red dust , ” he said and waited as the earth dissolved ,  and yet again ,  the silhouette reappeared in front of him. “From our sensors, it was a swarm of nanite machines . Its  purpose was to deconstruct any artificial construct on the planet ; once  done ,  the swarm eventually died . However ,  our records indicate a  substantial  growth of crystalline formations growing over the  earth  after that time, these formations then began to pulse with a frequency that has since interfered with our ability to document and record from the planet surface.  Again, Marcus paused, looking around he  finally  noticed small crystal growths on the trees and ground, the red, blue and green crystal spires seeming to grow on anything. He stepped over and  bent  down to study a spire, It looked harmless he thought and reaching out, touched it with his finger, just as quickly he pulled it away as if the rock had  bitten  him, slowly Marcus reached out again and touched the  stone , it thrummed as if power was coursing through the small rock, he could feel the vibration into his fingers and hand, After a moment he pulled his hand away, as he tried to count how many crystals he  could see, Marcus quickly lost count at a thousand, almost every tree had at least one he thought, such an invasive species and shaking his head he turned back to the VI “Are they powered, or are the crystals emitting some sort of signal” he asked .  Again  the VI paused as it communicated with the AI on his mothership.  “Yes to both questions, there is a sort of power emanating through them ,  but the source is unknown ,  and they are operating on a wavelength, sending out  a low-level communication , though it is too low to reach orbit and only seems effective up to a thousand feet from the crystal itself, the signal is constant ,  so it is more of a simple hum then anything intelligent” Sentinel finished.  Marcus shook his head again ,  looking back to the crystal, that was an interesting mystery, but one outside of his expertise ,  he thought. “Sentinel why launch random pods after the initial exodus?” he asked, remembering the lone pods launched over time. He waited for a response. “Due to a malfunction, over thirty pods remained on the ship, as they were repaired, they were then launched and returned to earth, as of this time twelve of the thirty have returned  over  three centuries” the VI finished .  Marcus paused for a moment, was it even possible he wondered . Finally ,  he found his voice ,  "Sentinel, what is the reason for the timeframe, surely it has not taken that long to fix twelve pods?” He queried.   The VI paused, this time longer than  usual ,  when it came back ,  the silhouette shrugged in a very human manner that caused Marcus  almost to take a step  back at the action. “That is unknown, the answer to that question is not available beyond  administration-level  access” Sentinel stated, and Marcus narrowed his eyes, since when did a repair get  top-level  access only, he wondered.  “Sentinel, who authorized the change in security for the repair information?” he asked and again waited for the machine’s answer .  “That information is not available beyond  administration-level  access , ” the  VI  stated. Marcus shook his head ; he  would have to look at that later, this brought up other issues he thought. “Sentinel, I assume the last pod to return was mine ; what  is the timeframe from the exodus to my pod returning to the planet , ” he asked, but he had seen the briefing and new well he wouldn’t like the answer.  After a moment ,  Sentinel came back “Two hundred twelve years since  the  exodus , ” she said, and it felt as if the breath  were  knocked  from  his chest ,  and Marcus stumbled back. Two hundred years, people have been on the planet for two centuries ,  he thought, and he was just now returning, what the hell happened ,  he wondered. More importantly, where was everyone ? Why  had no one come to welcome him ? He  wondered,  Reviewing options,  he nodded and queried Sentinel again.  “Sentinel, can you scan the surrounding area for populations, civilization or communication of any kind,  the  purpose is to find a concentration of people” he finished and waited with bated breath as the VI paused, communication with the ship and gathering those results.  Sentinel returned quicker than he expected .  “Marcus ,  because of the interference, I am unable to lock on any location of a human population . However,  I can tell you that there are no communications either over this location or the entire North American continent ; no  digital or analog broadcasts detected  since the exodus, ” Sentinel stated, again causing Marcus to pause in an alarmed panic.  How can that be he thought, people have been back for two hundred years, with the supplies and expertise of the twenty thousand people returned, surely there would be some sort of civilization he wondered, the information bothering him. Were there still people left ,  he wondered, could the effects of the machine have lasted causing those that returned to have died his mind continued.  That’s not helpful he chastised himself beginning to pace, he needed a plan, he couldn’t stay out here in the woods waiting for someone to come and get him. He was no survivalist ; he  was a damn engineer ; aside  from basic classes ,  he had no real ability to survive in the woods for long  periods ,  he thought, suddenly thinking maybe he should have gone to ranger school when he had the change.  After a few minutes of pacing ,  he had not come up with anything that could even be considered  a plan. With a sigh he turned back to the VI “Sentinel, based on the current information do you have a suggestion for a course of action that will allow me to learn the disposition and possibly reconnect with the population on the planet” he asked and with a mental wince, waited for the answer. A moment later the VI nodded “Marcus, based on the limited information we have it is my suggestion that the first place to stop would be the supply bunkers, you have limited supplies ,  and since it could some time to local others, you will need to ensure your ability to survive” The VI stated calmly . Marcus  could have slapped himself on the forehead.  The bunkers he thought remembering the briefing on the caches of supplies that would be left, the building  blocks  of the new  world ,  the  engineers and scientists bragged about them, proudly announcing the contents and location of the complexes.  The ARC founders knew that Earth would be in ruins ; they  built and supplied the bunkers to ensure  those   who  returned could use these locations as the building blocks of society.  The bunker  was  a great  first step he reflected nodding to the VI, he would go to the place they had gone ,  and if  Marcus  didn’t find supplies, he would at least have the starting point of the path he would have to take.  Marcus knew it was a long shot ; he  was ten centuries late to the party, it was possible  the bunkers  would be empty, but maybe there would be a clue as to where the volunteers had done. Either way ,  he thought, it was a good idea ,  “Sentinel, prepare to guide me to the closets bunker , ” Marcus commanded and began to collect his supplies.  As day became dusk ,  Marcus dropped the heavy pack, enjoying the release of the heavy burden he had been lugging around all day.  He leaned  against the bark of a tree  watching  as the VI casually walked over  to stand  next time him, silent it awaited orders. He knew the little ball floated, merely projecting the image of the woman, but it looked so real he thought studying the VI’s profile as it stood there, He would have to remember she wasn’t a real person, not a companion but merely a tool he thought.  For the entire day ,  he had followed the damn VI as they navigated the forest westward towards the closest bunker to his  ship's  landing site. He had covered the  vessel  with dead branches, doing his best to hide it, he wasn’t sure from what or whom, but it seemed like a good idea at the time he thought, but the exertion of doing that on top of walking made him rethink his earlier decision. “Sentinel, when will we reach the bunker , ” he asked, playing his own little game of ‘are we there yet’ with the machine.  “We will reach the bunker tomorrow” Sentinel stated, Marcus ,   nodded  absently, erecting  the small tent  and  rustling up dinner , as he stood over the fire cooking the little lump of food,  a rustling above caught his attention.  Standing ,  he pulled the hatchet and scanned the canopy as more branches shivered with movement. Something was up there ; he  thought taking a step back, never taking his eyes off of the tree.  He almost jumped out of his skin when a black tendril broke free of the densely covered branch and took off across the expanse towards another tree, stopping halfway and simply hovering as it waited for something. Marcus stood there, his jaw agape and the hatchet forgotten as he studied the creature, now fully displayed in the waning sunlight of the day.  “Sentinel, can you scan that creature” he whispered and waited as the VI put its palm up, virtual windows appearing into existence as the device began to scan the area leaving Marcus to study it. It is a snake he thought, following the black scaly body, which measured about six feet in length, ending at a narrow snakes head, that wasn’t what bothered him he reflected, his eyes now focusing on the  bat-like  wings sprouting from halfway along its body, the membranous wings lazily flapping as they cupped the air, keeping the animal in the air. “What the hell” he breathed, not able to take his eyes from the creature.  “Marcus, it appears to be some kind of hybrid animal, it is not the only one as others of its kind are close by, I would say from the number that this is not a fluke ,  but a mutation in the animal, one that  has evolved to become the species” Sentinel stated, loud enough to startle the creature and send it flying   into the far tree line, just as quickly about ten more erupted from the first tree and joined it, the flock moving at a fast speed to join its compatriot. “Well ,  it seems some things have changed since my last time here , ” he said half astonished and half smiling at his weak joke.  The sun was reaching mid-day as Marcus stood staring down into yet another large hole. “Where are we ,  Sentinel?” He asked ,  studying the crater-like pit. His eyes  roved  over yet more crystal spires looking for any sign of the supply filled bunker that should have stood on this very spot. For a few moments ,   Sentinel  stood stalwart before moving again towards the large mound of dirt .  “The bunker is directly in front of us based on the coordinates in the system , ” she said ,  floating up the berm, Marcus scrambled to follow.  His head felt as if it were trying to explode, the closer he got to the bunker the worse the pain was, wincing he climbed the small slope to the crest of the hill, doing his best to ignore the heavy beating drum in his forehead, what the hell is this he thought rubbing at his temples as he crested the hill.    At the top ,  he stood there looking over the expanse and  marveling  at the large hole filled to the brim with crystal spires, all colors and all sizes, spires reaching from the deep pit towards the sky, as if someone had lined the entire thing with spikes to kill a giant he thought staring in disbelief at the sheer amount of the rocks.  “This is not possible, according to my coordinates ,  this is the location of the closest bunker Marcus , ” Sentinel stated, her palm outstretched as she began gathering readings from the enormous collection of crystals.  Marcus merely sat on the edge ,  rubbing  at the pain  in his head ; what  the hell is that he wondered ,  squinting at the large hole of colorful rocks. After a moment ,  he  retreated  down the side of the hill ,   walking  a small distance from the  crater-sized  hole,  the pain ebbed, getting better the further from the spires he went . Finally,  it had calmed enough where he could think again . He  stopped taking a breath and saying a silent  thank you  as he waited for Sentinel .  Finally ,  once he had reached a distance where he could begin to think Marcus began to pace, he was a problem solver, his abilities relied  upon  recognizing patterns others missed ,  and something in the back of his mind was going off, was it something that sentinel had said that morning he wondered, continuing to wear a track in the forest floor as he concentrated on what he had learned from the machine over the past few days.  There was something there about the crystals and power, something about a signal, that might explain the feeling in his head, was it possible that he could sense the  energy   of  the signal, similar to some who were able to sense powerlines the closer they came to them he wondered. He was  sidetracking  himself and knew it, that wasn’t what was bothering him. Finally pausing in  mid-pace , he turned to the VI image “Sentinel, didn’t you say that the crystals appeared after the dissipation of the red nanite swarm?” he asked, knowing there was a correlation there, pulling on the thread of thought, he tried to follow it to its conclusion.  After a  momentary  pause ,  the VI returned “Yes Marcus, why do you ask?” it queried, with a simple nod he continued to pace, continued to think through the thought as it began to coalesce in his mind. “Sentinel scan the makeup of the crystals in that crater and then match it to the known chemical components of what would have been in that bunker , ” Marcus stated, crossing his fingers that he was wrong. It took almost fifteen minutes before the VI returned .  “It was not easy, the crystals themselves making remote scanning next to impossible, but this unit was able to collect enough local data to do an extrapolation” it began as Marcus waited impatiently for his answer. “According to the scan, the chemical makeup of the crystal collection matches that of the makeup of the building and supplies within the bunker at  eighty-seven  percent , ” Sentinel finished and waited for Marcus’s next command.  Blowing out a breath ,  he eyed the trees around him ,  seeing the crystal growths, and finally knowing what he was looking at, what those beautiful monoliths represented. “Sentinel, I think we are  looking at what was left of the human race, I think we are seeing what happened to the components of every building, monument, food wrapper and who knows what else that the swarm destroyed, I think these crystals are the tombstone to our race” he finished still eyeing the crystals. Sentinel did not respond,  simply  stood there waiting for the next order, despite the epiphany that Marcus had just laid on them both.  Suddenly he felt tired, drained of whatever energy remained in him, sitting down he hung his head, thinking of all that had been taken from this world, taken from him as he continued to stare at the  innocent-looking  crystal. As he sat there, a movement caught his eye, looking to his left he watched as a small  number  of crystal spires began to move through the forest floor, he couldn’t believe it, was it possible that the crystals themselves were alive he wondered, slowing getting up and watching as the mound continued to move. He crept over, slowly as the  pile  moved once again, making his way over, Marcus peered down into the  semi-tall  grass and began to laugh, under the mound of crystals rose a very familiar site, the heard of a turtle rising from beneath the ornate shell. “That’s a lot of bling ,  my friend , ” he laughed ,  shaking his head. The turtle did not seem impressed with his observation and continued to move towards the safety of the trees as Marcus continued to study the crystal shell. “Sentinel , ” he called ,  and the VI walked over to stand next to him “Can you scan this, is this shell covered with crystal growths?” he asked . Sentinel  stooped down, running its hand over the shell as new windows appeared in midair, listing information and graphs, the data transmitted to the ship, analyzed ,  and then returned. Sentinel stood and turned to Marcus .  “It appears that the shell is crystal Marcus after a quick scan it appears that this creature’s DNA has been altered as was the snakes , ” it stated. That alone wiped the smile from his face ; were  the crystals somehow changing the animal life on the planet ,  he wondered, then recalled the changes to his own body that the ARC project had propagated in order to allow him and all. The volunteers to survive cryogenic sleep, changes that had gotten from biological compounds found within the  machine, the device  an actual  merging of biology and electronics .  Fear  began to nibble at the edges of his conscious mind, pulling on the thread he turned hesitantly to the VI. “Sentinel, I need you to scan my body . Specifically,  my genetic makeup has anything changed since being put into stasis?” Marcus asked and then waited as Sentinel ran its holographic palm over his body and paused ,  awaiting the results.   After a few minutes ,  Sentinel spoke ,  “ According to the scan results, the biological component added to your body  to  make  cryo  sleep feasible was not slowed by the process as was the  rest of  your  body.   I t has since mutated merging with your DNA and  altering it, from my scan  you  are, even now continuing to change based on the mutation ”  Sentinel Stated and Marcus felt as if someone had punched him in the gut, this would explain some of the odd happenings . Still, what  was the result he wondered ,  fighting back the fear and  disgust  that was beginning to set in.  “ Sentinel, extrapolate the changes that have occurred and give me a best guess on  the roadmap of changes and what that will look like , ” he  asked  and again waited,  hoping it was benign at best . Sentinel returned after a time “ It is difficult to map  the full scope of  changes ; it  appears as if your body is developing a new sense, the ability to  receive and send signals on the same wavelength at the crystal spires ” Sentinel finished .  Marcus  winced again ;  his mind was changing ,  and he had known it, felt it, tried to ignore it, but somehow he was gaining an ability to talk to the  invasive rocks t hat now peppered his planet, what did  that  mean?  What  was there  a  purpose ? He  wondered ,  staring at the beautiful gems around the base of the closest tree .  That brought up a few unpleasant thoughts he reflected “Sentinel, based on the information you have at the time communications were cut off from Earth, did they surmise a function for the machine?” he asked. Thinking he knew what they would have found. “Yes ,  Marcus, according to the. Records, the final theory prior to communications  ending ,  was that the device was not a weapon at all, but an advanced tera former” she finished.  Whatever had built the damn thing thought Marcus had set it upon his planet to ensure that it  would eventually be habitable for their form of life, why so long he wondered,  evidently  with the technology that he had seen, the machine. Could have simply altered the planet and the species, why go through slow changes he wondered. He had a few theories but nothing he could prove, besides he had more  critical  problems ,  he thought.  Marcus  set up  camp once again, but instead of settling in, he began pacing, he had to find people, had to find out what happened to original volunteers, had they succeeded . There  was a civilization for him to return to , or had they simply died off, leaving Marcus the sole heir to humanity. He wondered.  He paced most of the afternoon ,  trying to solve the problem of the sensors . Still, the  more he thought about it ,  the more frustrated he became,  Marcus  was a mechanical engineer, not a damn software engineer  if there was a problem that required the sensors to be calibrated, he wasn’t the man to do it, he admitted slumping down in defeat next to the tent.  As the sun settled behind the horizon, the autumn air grew a bite as it became colder.  He huddled next to the warm fire lost in his thoughts as he studied the flames playing amongst the blackened pieces of wood. He had no way of leveraging the ship in orbit to find fellow humans ; he  would  have  to wander until, if he was fortunate, find a farm or town where the ARC members had  assembled , finding  there  children’s children. He looked down at the  large  can of smuggled food, knowing his supplies would run out long before he found such a place,  Marcus  needed to find an alternative means of supplying himself, bottom line he thought, I need to learn to hunt if I don’t want to starve. The cans had not been  a  standard-issue  but frozen in  a  vacuum ; they  would not go bad so, he and a few others had snuck them in  before  packing the bags for the trip. He recalled the night that he and a few others laughing at threw in the can’s, thinking they would share them once they had awoken. Sitting alone ,  he grew deeper into depression at the thought of those few people now long dead, centuries ago ,  and yet here he sat, alone and eating.  He lay leaning against a tree, the final embers of the firelight casting shadows across the ground and tent as if a kabuki show were in progress for his entertainment.  His body, still recovering from his long slumber compounded by the stress of his situation and the constant walking ,  made him want to crawl into a hole and rest .  Again , he  couldn’t do that ,  so he closed his eyes ,  mustering his remaining will power and energy. He had to push on, had to find people or he would do. His limited supplies were a constant worry ; soon,  he thought I am going to need to find a solution to my food problem.   If he were honest with himself, he was scared, scared of being alone,  afraid  of being the last human on earth, fated to wander the wilderness until he died. That thought did not sit well with him ; he  had been lost in his thoughts when a light shot above him, moving from branch to branch and catching his attention. He knew he was dead, knew his only salvation would be to reach the surface as his world narrowed, all other problems a distant thought as he pulled at the water, desperately trying to reach the murky light.  His chest was on fire as his arms pulled and pulled at the water, trying to fight the strong current, he could feel the edges of his world going black , the oxygen in his lungs now gone, his body fighting for the  life-giving  supply just feet above him. He felt himself getting weak, his vision going dark when suddenly he felt his hand break the surface, with all of the strength he had remaining he pulled because his life depended on it . Before  his vision went black ,  his head broke the surface ; he  sucked in  the  air until he could hold no more, his body involuntarily gasping over and over as he fought to keep himself above the rapids. He began to regain control, treading water he oriented himself towards the far shore, as he spun, he caught the sight of the Wolves, standing on the edge of the shore further back as the rapids had carried him further then he thought it would have.  The  Mother stood there looking towards Marcus, giving him that detached  look only a predator could , her two cubs tore apart the pack with gusto,  Marcus  pushed the thought out of his mind, one problem at a time he chanted realizing  his supplies were gone .  Marcus paddled to the far shore, fighting the rapids and struggling to keep himself above water. After what seemed like an eternity ,  his hand found solid ground ,  and he crawled up onto the rocky shore, collapsing in a heap of exhaustion. Marcus lay there for a time, his body cold he curled into a fetal position, he knew  he had to move, knew he would die if he stayed here. He had to get warm, had to dry his clothes ,  but he didn’t move, his body too heavy ,  so he just lay there, waiting for the inevitable.  A voice pulled him from his malaise “Marcus, your chances of survival are deteriorating fast, you need to get warm, your body is going into  hyperthermic  shock, you need to fight it .”  Snapping his head up ,  he could see Sentinel standing there not two feet away, looking down at him with a maternal like concern.  “Fuck off VI , ” he mumbled at the machine. He stayed there for a short time ; it  wasn’t the words or his  motivation that finally caused him to move ; it  was the  full-body  quakes that pulled him from the shore.  I will not die here; I will not let this place kill me  the thoughts echoing in his mind as he pulled himself towards the edge of the woods. He had to get warm, the VI is right he thought, his arms pulling the dry leaves and small branches into a pile in front of him, he reached as far as his body would allow and pulled more, the  collection  getting bigger as he  drew  everything he could into it.  He needed to get warm and dry ,  he thought, staring blankly at the pile of wood and kindling he tried to recall what he had been doing,  a  fire he thought, light the fire. Moving his leg ,  he felt a weight in his pocket, reaching down with a trembling hand he pulled out the binoculars, saying a small thank you ,  he began to remove the lenses.   “Marcus, if you do not get warm and dry ,  you will not survive” came the calm ,  gently voice of sentinel as his hands slipped from the cap as yet another set of convulsions took over his body ,  making it  next to impossible to disassemble the field glasses.  “Shut up ,  Sentinel, you’re not helping , ” he said through gritted teeth, finally getting the lens off of the binoculars. He closed his eyes, steadying himself as he held the lens out, catching the light he began to shift it until a small pinpoint of light displayed on the pile in front of him. The  tiny  sliver of light shaking as he tried unsuccessfully to hold his hand still, with a curse ,  he took a breath and tried again, steadying the light and focusing the power of the sun onto the pile.  A small whiff of smoke began to rise from the edge of a leaf ,  and he gently blew on it, watching the small leaf caught fire, excited he began to gently continue to  breathe  oxygen across the pile nurturing the small flame and encouraging it to grow. He crawled as close as he dared, the  little  pile growing quickly as the  warmth  of the flames began to thaw his body, Marcus lay like that for hours, moving only to find the closest things he could burn to throw on the fire.  Day turning to night as he continued to stay close to the burning pyre . His  mind barely present, his body trying to recover from the freezing water and cold weather. Eventually ,  Marcus drifted off to sleep, curled into a tight ball he did his best to stay warm as his mind drifted off. The sound  began in his head, at once he knew where he was ,  Marcus  opened his eyes to the view of the rocky cliffs, listening he could hear the thrumming once again, was it closer? he wondered ,  listening for a moment as the thrumming beat continued its death march over the horizon. “Something is wrong fallen one, I can sense it, what has happened” came the concerned voice of the woman from behind him. Something about that voice he thought, her question was more of a command he thought turning to find the same blonde-haired beauty in that red velvet dress, standing there tall and  majestic  in the field of tall grass only mere feet from him.  The look on her face was that of worry though ; this  is new he thought studying that face, what about this woman scared him he wondered as once again the hairs on his neck stood up in warning. He stood there for a moment studying this woman, after a moment he put on his best reassuring smile “Nothing at all, what is it you want lady, how is it you can contact me like this?” he said, switching the conversation in hopes of getting answers.  She too looked up, studying his eyes, searching them  she knows I am lying ,  he thought, it wasn’t  fear, the woman did know  he could feel it, could sense her conviction of that simple fact. She stopped studying him and smiled “I see you feel it, you cannot hide your intention here, you cannot obfuscate your intentions, all is known between those who use the mind bridge to communicate” she stated smiling at him.  Mind Bridge ,  he thought ,  pulling the word apart  some sort of telepathy  he wondered.  “What has happened Fallen One, let me help you , tell me where you are” the woman insisted, except now Marcus could feel more than the words . Still, the  intention as well, she  genuinely  was worried ,  but it was not worry for another person, no it was something else and not something he understood or could put his finger on . Still, his  instincts once again screamed at him, railed against the border of his mind, something about her was wrong he thought, something about what she is showing me, what she is telling me is not true ,  and my mind knows it, understands an intent or instinct I cannot consciously sense he thought.  He stood there for a moment trying to get his bearing, to process this new information and ability and as he did, he could feel her holding back, she wasn’t telling him everything,  so let’s take this mental shit for a test drive  he thought. “What do you want with me?” he asked directly and waited, the woman looked at him confused “To find you, to help you, to protect you , ” she stated.  The words sounded genuine, this woman did want to find him that was true, but it wasn’t to protect him, wasn’t to help him he thought feeling the intent flow off of the words, the sensation was impossible to describe it was like tasting colors, you had no idea what it felt like until you did it.   Something in the woman shifted as her eyes narrowed in suspicion ,  “Why won’t you let me help you?” she asked . Still, any  sense of care or comradery was now gone ; her  tone was  harsh ,  her words an accusation ,  and Marcus took an involuntary step back as his mind again screamed in fear. The  woman pressed, stepping forward ,  putting herself within his personal space .  “I will find you fallen one, save me the time and aggravation , ” she said, and he could sense the truth on those words.  “Who the fuck  are  you ,  lady?” Marcus spat   using anger to hide his fear, hoping to put her off balance . Still, it  didn’t work ; she  just smiled “I am the one who will save this world fallen one, I will use whatever tools I can to ensure that we are not  a  victim to that which your people let kill us, now tell me where you are” she finished her voice raising to scream on the last phrase . Marcus  stepped back, trying to put space between them, as he did, his food found dead air ,  and he remembered too late the cliff as he toppled, falling over the edge and speeding towards the water and rocks below.  Marcus jerked awake ; relaxing ,   he took in the  familiar sight of the  camp ,  the biting cold settling  into his body  as he  noticed the smoldering curls of smoke from  what remained of the campfire .   C ursing he shakily stood, walking and picking up branches and leaves, the fire had almost died . The  pile of smoldering ash wasn’t enough to keep him warm. Returning to the fire ,  he built it back up , laying down on the small warm area of the earth he thought of the woman, she meant him  Marcus  had seen the intent in feeling emanating off of her words and for the first time he feared finding people, finding civilization.  A lot could have changed and seemed to have in the centuries since he had walked the earth, what would he find ,  and more importantly ,   was he in dan ger , His body slowly relaxed ,  and he returned to sleep reflecting on this and the lady by the cliff. He woke the next morning feel off, his body hurt everywhere ,  and a small tickle in the back of his throat refused to go away. After a few swallows of water, he forced himself to move. “Sentinel?” he said and could hear the rasp in his voice  this isn’t good  he thought, the last thing he needed now was to get sick and having spent time in the freezing water of the river and the autumn cold of night, it was looking more like his body wouldn’t recover quickly. “Yes ,  Marcus, how many I help you?” came the friendly voice of the VI ,  and he turned to find her behind him, standing patiently for his orders.  “Based on our new location, can you navigate us to the location we previously identified , ” he said ,  rubbing his temples as a headache threatened to go from bad to worse.  The VI paused ,  and he waited as she communicated with the ship, looking around Marcus realized he was hungry ,  and then the events of yesterday hit him.  “Fuck , ” Marcus whispered ,  remembering the pack strewn over the rocks, the wolves tearing through it with gusto, his supplies eaten or destroyed .  Marcus had never been one to enjoy hunting ; it  wasn’t anything against the sport ; just  it was easier to go to the grocery store. Looking around the lush forest ,  he now found a new appreciation for that skill.  He  groaned at the irony of his current predicament.  Checking his belt ,  his hands came upon the sturdy handle of the K-Bar ,  and he sighed ,  “Okay, I can do this , ” he said ,  going over his options as he studied the forest with new eyes, that of an engineer with a problem to solve.    Sentinel returned “Marcus ; we  are still able  to navigate to the location easily , the river will not pose an issue in our travels” she stated , at least one thing wasn’t going to be an issue he thought.  An  idea began to form as  Marcus  studied  the surrounding forest.  “Sentinel, can you find an offshoot of the river, slower rapids, something close by , ” he  asked . Two hours later,  Marcus  stood   knee-deep  in a slow traveling tributary, holding his breath  watching  the water intently ,  Sentinel  floated close by “Based on the reference material we have access to, you will need to stay quiet and still, the fish will soon get used to your presence, wait until they are close before you use the spear, jabbing it straight down should garner a fish”  she  stated . Marcus  shot it an annoyed look .  “Yes, I know, quiet , ” he whispered.  The spear in question was a stick that he had sharpened one end, the word spear was probably too grand for the simple stick, but it was what he had Marcus thought studying the water  carefully . Despite the pain in every muscle and joint ,  he kept himself still, watching the water, trying to see under the surface as the sun distractedly played over the ripples in the surface ,  making the task daunting. The  only sound was the water lapping against the shore, the effect calming as  Marcus  continued to stand there .   T ime passed as he frustratingly watched large  silverfish  pass just out of reach, oblivious to the danger and his irritation as he watched them saunter by again and again.  Close  to giving up,  Marcus  was in the middle of rethinking his position when he looked down to see a  giant   silverfish , floating just below him .   Sing  his legs to break the wake . It  just floated there, not moving as it seemed interested in something on his pants and moved in, nipped at it ,  and then backed off.  Standing  there in shock ,   Marcus  stared at the fish ,  finally   recalling   his hunger,   he tightened his grip on the stick, carefully aiming  and then   slammed the stick  into its target. With a smile and a cheer ,  Marcus pulled the  rod  from the water ,  the  giant  fish speared through the end. “Hell yeah , ” he screamed to the woods, startling a flock of birds from the trees.  After eating the overcooked fish and with a smile and a full belly ,  he started , following the VI through the thick forest as he headed towards civilization. Using the  ship's  ability to map the journey ,  he was able to stay near sources of water ,  allowing him to fish, but by the fifth day ,  the tickle and aches in his body had grown worse. Sitting by the fire one night as the sun had set, he stared at the flames, his body launching into a coughing fit, his sides lighting up in pain as he tried to expel whatever was in his lungs.  After it subsided ,  he pulled his hand back to reveal bloody mucus “This isn’t a good sign” he whispered, for the first time since the wolves Marcus thought  he  might not make it, might end up dying before he could make contact with others, before he could see what had become of his world and his people. The fever was causing him to sweat, but as soon as it touched the air ,  it would  grow  cold ,  causing him to shiver, he couldn’t get warm no matter how close he got to the fire.  Three days he traveled, barely saying a word, a zombie  merely  putting one foot in front of the other as the fever continued to get worse, he had stopped eating, his only sustenance was the water he forced down his throat twice a day. One foot in front of the other, he thought  trying  to keep himself moving despite the pain and confusion in his mind. He walked and walked trying to keep the fear and panic of death at bay, his mind whispering to him, telling him to rest, surely death couldn’t be as bad as this it said, but Marcus ignored it, cursed it even yelled at it ,  but still it refused to go away. Mercifully the vision of the cliffs had not come again,  though  that could have been from his inability to sleep more than anything else he thought in one of his more lucid moments.  Marcus had stopped tracking time and distance, merely walking becoming his whole existence, he had stopped talking to Sentinel ,  who simply floated in front, leading him . As  he faltered, the VI would slow ,  ensuring she was always directly in his path, a beacon to salvation.  I am going to die ,  he thought as they traveled, he didn’t know how far they had come or how close they were, but it didn’t matter, Marcus knew he would not make it. The fever had gotten worse ,  his walking  faltering  into  stumbling .  Shuffling forward,  his eyes focused  at the ground ,  his mind  trying  to decide if  lying  down, giving in would be so bad .   S uddenly the sun became brighter as the trees opened up above, surprised Marcus stopped looking up and then around, something about this called to him, tried to get his attention . Still, his  mind was muddy, unable to form a clear thought ,  and so he stood there staring blankly around as his body swayed.  A sound started in the distance, something hitting the ground ,  and he cocked his head was that  a sound or something his mind had created ,  he wondered. It wasn’t the first time since becoming sick that his mind had played tricks on him, he thought ,  closing his eyes, listening to the sound as it began to grow progressively louder.  There was something familiar about it ,  he thought listening intently as his body continued to sway with fever, he had heard that before, but where. Turning ,  he caught sight of motion ,  and his eyes went wide, his mind trying to process the sight as two horses with riders bore down on him. They rode  fast as he continued to just stand there his fever addled mind not able to process the sight ,  and then just as quickly they passed, one turned and called back something in a language he didn’t understand ,  but the sentiment was clear.  “Help” he tried to call, his voice a raspy whisper as the riders disappeared around the bend, looking down he noticed the worn ground, a simple dirt road, this had been what had stopped him, his unconscious mind understanding the meaning before he did. There are people near he thought as adrenaline coursed through his system, his body responding to the hope that erupted in his mind like a nuclear explosion. He wasn’t going to die, Marcus turned and saw sentinel, waiting ,  and he approached, following the VI, knowing now he had to make it, had to find someone to help. So, he walked, noticing the old derelict fence shadowing him as he walked up the worn dirt road. As the sun began to settle ,  he came over a hill . He stopped , the sight bringing a tear to his eye as in the distance, stood a simple wood cabin surrounded with small pens for animals and fields stretching far into the distance, a farm he thought , picking up his pace, moving towards the first sign of salvation since landing. As the small home grew closer ,  he noticed the  hand-laid  shingles and simple poles holding up a crooked porch . H e  studied the old  two-story  barn and the pens holding familiar animals like cows and pigs ,  the sight bringing a smile to his face as he turned into the open gate of a mostly fallen property fence and made his way to the door.  Stepping onto the porch ,  he made his way to the large wooden door to the salvation that existed beyond. The boards protested at the weight as he moved onto the porch. Pausing for a moment ,  he turned to the hologram standing next to him “ It’s  probably better if they don’t see you Sentinel, we have no idea how they will react , ” Marcus rasped as the image of the woman instantly vanished .   T he small  egg-shaped  machine rising into the rafters and out of sight. Marcus reached  out,  feeling the weight of the wood as he knocked three times.  He could hear the sound echo through the area, judging by the lights in the windows, someone was home . Then  he  listened to  the sound of movement , someone slowly approached the door, pausing for a moment ,  and Marcus thought he could hear breathing and listened  as Metal scraped metal ,  and the large door opened a crack, revealing a large blue eye of a woman.  For a moment ,  Marcus was lost, he didn’t know what to say and simply stood there gawking at another human, tears now freely streaming down his cheeks.  Finally, he took a step forward .  “Help me, please, I am sick , ” he said and took another step towards the heavy door. Suddenly it shut ,  and he heard the movement of the locks as the door was barred against him.  Marcus simply collapsed, he had no energy, no ability to do more as the sickness finally overwhelmed him, he drifted into  fevered darkness.
